column4: Identification of Biotransformation Products of 6PPD and 6PPD-Q
column5: Analysis of the pathways of 6PPD implied that it may undergo sequential enzymatic transformations catalyzed by glutathione S-transferases (GSTs), γ-glutamyl transferases (GGTs), UDP-glycosyltransferases (UGTs), and hexokinases (HKs).

column4: Identification of Biotransformation Products of 6PPD and 6PPD-Q

column4: Identification of Biotransformation Products of 6PPD and 6PPD-Q
column5: Among them, 6DTP431 likely arises from UGT-mediated glycosylation at a secondary amine, while the two 6DTP511 isomers reflect phosphorylation of the glucoside conjugates at distinct amine sites by HKs, consistent with phosphoglucoside formation observed for genistein and albendazole in C. elegans.
